items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007

ctx.x: You know that’s a good question. I can’t honestly give you an answer because I think if there’s a criticism of me it may be that I’m a little too eclectic. Or as George Bush says “echolectic.” Anyway — that’s whole ‘nother subject. So this eclecticism, I search for the not standard. You know I try to write things that maybe aren’t in the proverbial forms, or A-A-B-A. I search for those things that are slightly different that maybe I can put my imprint on that may be a little more individual. And sometimes that…

sometimes I fall back into the A-A-B kind of thing. But usually I’m looking for something that intrigues my sensibilities and then I feel that all music has to come through me to get to you. If it doesn’t intrigue me it’s going to come out at about three inches and fall to the floor. If I feel it, then there’s a good chance of me conveying that to you. So that’s how I feel about composition too, and melody and lyrics.
